app_tagline: Open Source Licenses & Version Control Architecture
hero_description: Without a license, default copyright laws apply. Choose the right open source license for your repository, understand public vs private trade-offs, and master the universe of .gitignore templates.
matrix_subtitle: Filter and compare permissions, conditions, and limitations across popular software licenses.
lic_mit_desc: A short and simple permissive license with conditions only requiring preservation of copyright and license notices. Unrestricted commercial reuse.
lic_apache_desc: A permissive license that also provides an express grant of patent rights from contributors to users, with trademark protection clauses.
lic_gpl_desc: Permissions of this strong copyleft license are conditioned on making available complete source code of licensed works and modifications under GPLv3.
lic_bsd_desc: A permissive license similar to the MIT License, but with a specific 3rd clause prohibiting endorsement using authors' names without permission.
lic_agpl_desc: Extended copyleft license closing the SaaS/cloud loophole by requiring source code disclosure to users interacting with the software over a network.
lic_unlicense_desc: A license with no conditions whatsoever which dedicates works to the public domain. Completely unrestricted for any personal or commercial use.
git_section_subtitle: Step-by-step repository initialization, public vs private repository comparison, and the complete .gitignore ecosystem.
git_step1_desc: Execute standard CLI commands to initialize, stage, commit, rename branch, and link to GitHub/GitLab remote.
git_step2_desc: Security, visibility, collaboration models, and CI/CD minutes quota evaluation for team governance.
git_step3_desc: From ActionScript and Ada to Node.js, Python, Rust, and Go, plus standard IDE and OS exclusion patterns.
footer_desc: Modern multilingual & themeable web architecture engineered with semantic HTML5, pure CSS3 variables, and vanilla ES6+ i18n logic.
